every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not

claims.claim: Vatalanib, which shares the pyridylmethyl-substituted fused heteroaromatic motif, has an absolute oral bioavailability of 58% in humans after a single dose.
Folic acid, whose pterin core closely matches the query's 2-amino-6-oxo purine, showed high bioavailability, with only about 10% of the dose excreted in ileostomy effluent.
Piritrexim, a fused pyrimidine with a methylene-linked aryl group, showed absolute oral bioavailability values of 23%, 43%, 63%, and ~75%, all at or above the 20% threshold.
Naratriptan, a fused pyrrole heteroaromatic, showed oral bioavailability of 63-74% across reported populations.
Isoniazid, a small pyridine-containing drug, showed oral bioavailability of 78% in fed and 93% in fasted patients.
Bromfenac showed absolute oral bioavailability of 67% ± 20% in healthy fasted subjects.
CP-409,092 showed a relative bioavailability of 69 (33)% from intravenous and oral clinical studies.
Nilotinib showed absolute oral bioavailability of 31% under fasted conditions, still above the 20% threshold.

evidence_gaps: No direct oral bioavailability measurement for the query molecule.
No experimental permeability or Caco-2 data for the query.
No human PK, metabolic stability, or transporter data for the query.
Tautomeric and ionization behavior of the guanine-like core is not experimentally characterized.
Oxipurinol card C07 is formulation-relative and does not provide an absolute F value.
content.decision_summary: All transferable L1 records show oral bioavailability at or above 20% (mostly 31-93%), including structurally related fused heteroaromatics (vatalanib, folic acid, piritrexim, naratriptan); no affirmative low-F evidence exists, so predict high.
